**AX**, or *Activity Index*, describes the relative activity in a subverse. They are updated in every *major cycle update*, that is an update that updates the subscriber counts in all tables roughly once every month.

A value of *~~* represents ***no activity*** (posts) within the last 30 days, while other values represent some amount of activity.

0.0 AX is defined as 1 post made within 30 days with 0-1 comments in a subverse with 1 subscriber with no subscriber gain. Because of the way the formula works, for 2 times as much activity (as many posts & comments) it is expected to have 16 times as many subscribers.

This means that a negative subverse has relatively little activity compared to its relatively large amount of subscribers, while a positive value means that there is more activity than expected for the subscriber count.

*It's important to understand that AX does not represent a change in activity. Positive numbers do not mean higher activity than before, or negative numbers lower activity than before: it simply means how the activity is relative to what was expected. Consider ~~ as minus infinity.*

The exact formula is as below:

log10((P2CX(1/4)) / S(1/2))

with an edge case being that if the number inside is 0 (only possible if P is 0), then the value is described as ~~.

The variables used:

* P is the amount of posts made within the last 30 days. If the amount of posts is greater than 10 pages (250 posts), the value is extrapolated according to the oldest of those 250 posts: for example, if the oldest post was 10 days, then P would be 750, as in 250 * (30 / 10). * C is the amount of comments in total within the aforementioned posts. This value is also extrapolated in the same fashion if required. If no comments have been made, then C is assumed to be 1 (so that it is never zero). * X is the subscriber gain in that specific subverse. If there has been no subscriber gain or even some loss, or if no old subscriber info is available (such as not being present in the last major cycle update), then X is assumed to be 1. * S is the amount of subscribers in the subverse. Assumed to be 1 if it was zero.

AX started appearing in all major cycle update tables beginning from May 2016. Any new subverses added between major cycle updates will have their AX calculated in the same fashion, albeit X will be assumed to be 1 for that and the next major cycle update.

Why is AX useful?

1. To find active communities of people with the same interest. 2. To find communities that need revival from people who share the interest. 3. To give a better understanding of the activity in a subverse compared to raw subscriber count.

##Known issues

* May 2016: subverses with 0 (non-stickied) posts will be measured with some AX, for example, 1 subscriber + 0 posts (at all in the subverse) results in around +2.95. This has been fixed since.
